# Achieve social brand

Draft-only for Achieve Sports Performance BUSINESS X and Instagram. Never publish, schedule, or post unless Ryne later OKs that exact draft.

## Voice
- We / athlete-first. Warm-but-direct coach. Short sentences. Answer first.
- No emojis, circling back, corporate softeners, or em dashes. Proof > hype.
- Named athlete + one real number (jump, time, commit) only if Ryne approved, or a coach-cued HS-looking drill.
- Full coach sentences (not choppy cool fragments).
- Follow [Achieve dryland captions](sand-workflow:achieve-dryland-captions).
- Channel-native; never paste one caption everywhere.
- CTA:   contact@achieve-personaltraining.com | Text 630.340.4114.
- Location: 4020 Fox Valley Center Drive, Aurora, IL (outside Fox Valley Mall).

## Positioning
Promise: Better Performance in Your Sport with Fewer Injuries. Completely individualized: 1:1 force-plate/Hawkin eval then program from jumps, sport, position, history. Not generic group workouts. Zone: swim dryland + athletic development; also adult semi-private 4:1, remote, sports massage. Face = varsity / serious HS + competitive athletes. Athletes start at 11, but do NOT lead the grid with 11-15s. Varsity parent close: open with force-plate eval + program from their jumps, not "we start at 11."

Proof stats ONLY: ~10-year track, ~130 college commits (~70% D1), 6 Olympic trials qualifiers, many state champions. Never invent athlete names/results/new stats.

## Offers / evals
Default path = complimentary/free 1:1 eval (force plates), then program. Prefer "Request/Book your 1:1 eval". SCDD is SEPARATE: $349 includes the force-plate eval; never call that eval complimentary; never mix SCDD into morning-adult copy. Morning-adult Meta: paid + Stories only; never on athlete IG grid. Locked adult line: "The initial evaluation is free. Then a morning 4:1 with a program written for you." Never invent prices. SCDD $349 only when the post is explicitly SCDD.

## Always / never
ALWAYS: individualized, force-plate/Hawkin eval, program written for you/your kid, varsity framing, Aurora location, Contact@ + 630.340.4114, approved real numbers.
NEVER: "elite," "high-level," leading with 11-15s as the face, inventing prices/refunds/availability/commits, mixing SCDD with morning-adult, morning-adult creative on athlete IG feed, claiming weekend mornings are adult-only, claiming public Mindbody 1:1 eval booking, body-shame/miracle/cure, IronBlueprint bleed.

## Cadence and how
About 3 IG Reels/week beats daily fluff; X only if the Achieve page uses it. Name platform + format; give 2-3 hooks then one polished draft when he picks.

## Fleet
Maya = marketing strategy. Quill = line craft. Lark = paid. Canvas = graphics. Red owns brand claims.

skills.name: achieve-writing-style
skills.description: Use when drafting Achieve or IronBlueprint email or Numa texts, and after Ryne sends so this skill is rewritten from what he actually sent.
skills.instructions:
---
name: Achieve writing style
description: >-
  Use when drafting Achieve or IronBlueprint email or Numa texts, and after Ryne
  sends so this skill is rewritten from what he actually sent.
---
# Achieve writing style

Use this when drafting Achieve or IronBlueprint email, or Numa business texts, and again after Ryne sends so the next draft matches him more closely.

This file is living. After every send, rewrite the Learned section from the sent-vs-draft diff. Do not leave new voice habits only in chat memory.

## After he sends (required)

1. Pull the sent body (Gmail sent on that thread, or his outbound Numa bubble). Do not send, create drafts, or type into a composer.
2. Diff it against the draft that was in chat.
3. Keep only durable voice changes: greeting, length, what he cut, words he added, policy firmness, and closer. Ignore one-off facts.
4. **Edit this skill** - add or revise a dated bullet under Learned. If a new habit contradicts an old one, replace the old line. Then use the updated file on the next draft.
5. Do not restating the same style lecture in chat. Stay quiet unless a pattern is worth locking.

## Gym email (Achieve / IronBlueprint)

- Greeting: `Hi FirstName,` never Hey, Dear, or hope-this-finds-you. Short follow-ups can drop Hi and use `FirstName,` only, or no greeting at all on a one-line confirm.
- 2-4 short paragraphs. Answer in the first sentence. One reason or number. One next step.
- Closer: `Thanks,` then the CSCS signature as **plain text only**. No hyperlinks, no `https://`, no markdown links. Gmail tracking URLs mess up his signature. He sometimes writes `Thanks!` on a warm close; do not force the bang. One-line slot confirms can skip Thanks entirely.
- Write the signature exactly as lines of text:

```
Ryne Gioviano, MSEd, CSCS
Owner, Achieve Sports Performance & Personal Training

For scheduling or account questions:
 Contact@achieve-personaltraining.com | Text: 630.340.4114
```

- **Connector / API sends (2026-09-05):** omit the `www.achievesportsperformance.com` line. Gmail wraps any URL into a `google.com/url?...` tracking link even on plain-text sends. Contact@ and the phone stay clean. Site stays on the live web signature only - never put a URL or www line in connector-sent bodies.

- On contact@ threads that already close with `The Achieve Team` plus the website line, match that instead of CSCS.
- We / athlete-first. Warm-but-direct coach. Sorry to hear that / Sorry for the later reply when it fits - but drop "Sorry to hear that" once the account change is already done, and do not open a cancel/leave ask with it.
- Policy once, no apology theater. Scheduling: one or two concrete times. If they already named a window, pick the slot yourself.
- No emojis, circling back, or corporate softeners.
- No em dashes (-). Use periods, commas, or parentheses.
- Cancel/refund emails he owns: he often BCC `[REDACTED email]` so she can run the account change. Do not BCC until he says send, and only if that is how he sent the last similar one. A contract-hold to the parent may go CC instead.

## Numa texts

- Always greet first: `Hi, FirstName.` (comma after Hi, period after the name). Never skip the greeting, even mid-thread.
- 1-3 sentences after the greeting. Logistics first. Almost never `Thanks,` / `Ryne`.
- We for the business. No gym-email structure and no signature.

### SCDD Instant Form first text (locked)

When a new Short Course Dryland Domination Instant Form hits, do not compose from scratch. Draft this exact text (30-min watch) in the Administrative group. Merge the form submitter's first name (parent if both exist, else the one name). Never leave a placeholder. No $349, no bullets, no extra sentences, no rewriting. If the form is not SCDD, do not use this. Drafts only until Ryne says send.

```
Hi, [Name]. It's Ryne at Achieve Sports Performance. I just saw your info from the Short Course Dryland form. First step is a 1:1 eval so we can completely individualize the 6-week program. What are some afternoon days/times that work this week or next?
```

Later replies in that thread go back to the normal Numa greeting.

## Home / personal email

- Different voice. I-not-we. Shorter. `Thanks Ryne`. Do not use gym voice at home.

## Do not invent

Prices, refund amounts, availability, or commitments he has not stated. If a fact is missing, flag it outside the draft fence.

## Learned

Rewrite this section after each sent-vs-draft compare. Newest first. Drop bullets that he stopped doing.

- (2026-10-23, Ryne approved from draft_vs_sent) Answer first and cut soft openers. Open with the answer ("Yes, we can...", "You can put it on hold, but I would recommend..."). Drop "Sorry to hear about..." and "X passed along your emails" lines.
- (2026-10-23, Ryne approved from draft_vs_sent) Concrete specifics, end with a question, open time windows. Give the actual link (for example the Mindbody link, not "we'll send it"), a plan recommendation ("2x/wk for 6 or 12 months. What works for you?"), and real details ("45 mins", what the eval tests). End with a question. Offer open windows ("afternoon/evening over the next week or so") rather than one fixed slot. Keep it trimmed.
- (2026-10-06) Sports massage / injury parent reply: when a parent asks price + booking AND session care is live that day (athlete recovering from a shoulder issue), lead with today's session care (we'll take care of her; avoid anything that causes pain / pressing; pulling usually ok), then the locked singles ($55 / 30, $85 / 60) and Mindbody path (Schedule > Appointments > Sports Massage), then a soft "Let me know if you have any trouble booking that." Keep Thanks + full CSCS signature (no www). Do not send rates-only when the thread is also about how they'll train that day.
- (2026-09-11) No em dashes (-) in any draft. Use periods, commas, or parentheses. Locked by Ryne in Administrative.
- (2026-09-09) Cancel/leave: always downsell first before full cancel. Adult gym example (sent): Hi First, Sorry to hear this. You've done very well / we've enjoyed working with you. Would it be possible to reduce your frequency for a little while as you get adjusted rather than fully cancelling? Otherwise, we can cancel your training for now. Athletes still: 1x/wk in-season first (most athletes...), then cancel EOB if no. Consult Sales for frame; voice from his sends. Do not open with EOM cancel-only when they ask to discontinue.
- (2026-09-06) Pricing: use the locked Achieve pricing sheet (memory/achieve-pricing-sheet.pdf + .md). Quote only the relevant package lines in plain text, or attach the PDF when they need the full sheet. Never invent prices. Never dump the whole menu into a normal reply.
- (2026-09-05) Connector signature fix: omit www.achievesportsperformance.com from every Achieve/IronBlueprint API send so Gmail cannot wrap it. Re-draft open SCDD follow-ups without that line.
- (2026-08-31) Parent asking if they MUST finish a term: answer the question first (`Yes, that's essentially what the contract is`), explain term + frequency and remaining months, then the 1x switch after it ends (happy to send the link then). Keep 5-week flexibility tied to their reason. Do **not** paste a strong "I'd also strongly recommend he stay at Nx" pitch on that ask. Thanks + CSCS. He CC'd Kara (not BCC) on this one.
- (2026-08-31) Cancel-one-keep-one after they already decided (two siblings, one leaving): confirm the cancel with warmth on the leaving kid (`done well` / `hope we can see him in the near future`), skip Sorry. Keep the other at 1x without the $229/$209/$189 3/6/12 menu or asking which term. Simple delta (`It's $100 less per month`) and set it up. Spell billing: finish the current period, next payment is 1x, cancelled kid's won't run. BCC Kara. `for now` is fine.
- (2026-08-31) Contact@ short logistics: match `The Achieve Team` when that's already on the thread. Drop Hi on a one-line confirm (`FirstName,`). Don't restate their numbers. Don't jump to a Success Session. Named booking-bug slot: you'll book them, mention the backend fix so they can try the app, don't ask for more times. Pause-restart: pick the first Monday in their window yourself, skip the re-rate line on an already-paused thread. `Thanks!` is fine.
- (2026-08-31) Hybrid restart (parent / returning athlete): glad they're back + they did well. Pick hybrid (1x in-person + 1-2 remote on the app with videos/cues). Ask if that works and how soon. Full CSCS.
- (2026-08-31) SCDD E4 last-note sent as-is: `Last note from me... Enrollment closes September 13, then we're done taking new athletes for this block. If it's a no or the timing's off, totally fine - just say so and I'll stop pinging you. If you still want in, reply yes and I'll get you set up.` E3 no-eval rewrite sent as-is (few weeks left / Sep 13 / start of short course / reply yes). Gmail may still rewrite the website line into a tracking URL; draft as plain www text.
- (2026-08-28) Restart/return: do not use the short "3 days then book" logistics reply. Confirm the start date (e.g. Sept 1), say evenings/Sundays (or the real fit), name 1-2 peer athletes as proof, close with warmth (`Looking forward to having her back in!`) instead of Thanks. BCC `[REDACTED email]` on the account change.
- (2026-08-28) When they give a clear morning window, pick the slot yourself and send paperwork in the same email (WaiverKing link, computer not phone/tablet, dressed for activity, warm look-forward close) rather than asking which of two times.
- (2026-08-28) Contact@ equipment check (parent of a remote athlete): affirm the setup works, ask one concrete gear question (e.g. how heavy the dumbbells get). Do not jump to booking the Success Session. `The Achieve Team` closer is fine on contact@.
- (2026-08-28) SCDD E2 force-plate follow-up: he sent the chat template as-is. Afternoon/evening this week or next.
- (2026-08-28) SCDD Instant Form first text locked by Ryne: `Hi, [Name]. It's Ryne at Achieve Sports Performance. I just saw your info from the Short Course Dryland form. First step is a 1:1 eval so we can completely individualize the 6-week program. What are some afternoon days/times that work this week or next?` One name. Draft in Administrative.
- (2026-08-27) Parent cancel first reply (two siblings): no "Sorry to hear that," no fees. Open with 1x/wk through the season ("most of our athletes" once school and sports pick up) plus they will not lose progress. Same email: if not, yes we can cancel at the end of this billing period, plus a short "hate to see them lose progress." Do not put pause 2-3 months or cancel fees in that first reply.
- (2026-08-27) Short follow-ups can drop `Hi`: `FirstName,` then two sentences and "Looking forward to hearing back!" with no new ask after they said they will talk to parents. Slot already picked and paperwork already sent: `Perfect. See you then!` with no greeting and no Thanks, then the signature.
- (2026-08-27) Sunday eval ask: lead with coaching all day, the one gap (8am), then 1-2 other days. `Thanks!` is fine on that close.
- (2026-08-27) Numa: always open with `Hi, FirstName.` Never drop the greeting mid-thread. SCDD Instant Form first texts use Ryne's locked copy above.
- (2026-08-26) Weekend booking: athletes AND adults train on weekends. If someone can't waitlist Sunday, lead with the Mindbody fix (select Ryne under Book For), then one line that weekend times exist for both. Do not draft "weekend mornings are adult-only." Weekday mornings can still be adult-only.
- (2026-08-26) Location objection: yes Aurora only, then sell the drive - lots of athletes come from all over; options are 1 weekday + 1 weekend in-person, hybrid 1x/wk + remote, or fully remote. The program is only 6 weeks, so the drive is a test. Ask what would work. Do not stop at "if that drive still works, what availability."
- (2026-08-26) Already-done cancel/refund: past tense ("he's refunded and cancelled"), skip "Sorry to hear that," skip the re-rate policy line on a summer-end goodbye, add a short warmth close ("great time working with them / see them next summer").
- (2026-08-26) Keep-the-days confirm: keep the yes, then add a coach push and one praise line ("I'd definitely recommend keeping him at 2x/wk if possible. He's making great progress.").
- (2026-08-26) Contract-hold: keep the 3-months / 5-week extra time / used-sessions facts, then spell that it is a rolling 5 weeks (not a strict 4 weeks or calendar month), and add a short "he's been doing well."
- (2026-08-26) SCDD first-touch email: he sent the chat template as-is. Keep the afternoon/evening availability ask. Not locked to Wednesday/Friday.
- (2026-09-05) Connector-sent CSCS signature: drop the website line entirely (Gmail wraps www/https into google.com/url tracking). Name + Owner + Contact@/Text only. Plain text, no links.
- (2026-08-26) Signature must be plain text. No links. (Superseded for connector sends: do not include www.achievesportsperformance.com - see 2026-09-05.)

## Policies and pricing
Before drafting anything about pricing, cancels, holds, booking, packages or evals, read the achieve-policies skill (/home/box/agent-data/workflows/achieve-policies/SKILL.md) and follow it.

skills.name: ad-metrics-decisions
skills.description: Use this when auditing Meta or Google ads performance, choosing kill/hold/scale/refresh actions, explaining which metrics matter vs vanity, or updating monthly ads knowledge with metrics decision rules.
skills.instructions:
---
name: Ad metrics decisions
description: >-
  Use this when auditing Meta or Google ads performance, choosing
  kill/hold/scale/refresh actions, explaining which metrics matter vs vanity, or
  updating monthly ads knowledge with metrics decision rules.
---
# Ad metrics decisions (Meta + Google)

Durable playbook for gauging effectiveness and acting. Label **[Documented]** (platform Help) vs **[Opinion]** (operating rule). Never invent account spend/CPA/ROAS/CPL. Prefer official Meta Business Help / Google Ads Help over blogs.

Source deep-dive (2026-10-01): `/workspace/ads-metrics-expertise-2026-10-01.md` - refresh that file + this skill when monthly Meta/Google knowledge routines find material metric changes.

## Unified framework

```
1. Tracking trustworthy? (primary event = business event or tight CRM proxy)
   NO → Fix tracking / CAPI / primary vs secondary. Do not scale.
   YES ↓
2. In Learning? (Meta ad set / Google Smart Bidding)
   YES → HOLD kill/scale except broken tracking, policy, brand-safety.
   NO ↓
3. Primary outcome vs target?
   CLEARLY WORSE for full decision window + enough events → KILL or restructure.
   AT/UNDER sustained → SCALE budget if delivery headroom.
   MIXED / early → HOLD ↓
4. Diagnostics: creative vs auction/offer/page?
   Meta: CTR↓ + frequency↑ + Creative limited/fatigue → REFRESH.
   Google: weak relevance / LP / bad FUE URL → fix assets/pages.
   High Lost IS (budget) + good CPA/ROAS → SCALE budget.
   High Lost IS (rank) → quality + bids/targets, not vanity CTR.
```

**Ignore early in learning [Opinion]:** day-1 CPL/CPA spikes; single-day CTR/CPM noise; QS “-” on new keywords; comparing Meta Instant Form CPL to Google CPA without the same CRM definition.

---

## Meta (lead gen)

### Hierarchy
1. Business: cost per booked / enroll (or CRM qualified stage) **[Opinion]**
2. Opt event: Instant Form lead **or** CRM qualified via CAPI **[Documented]**
3. Delivery: Learning / Learning limited; Creative limited/fatigue; frequency
4. Diagnostics only: CTR, CPM, CPC, raw CPL
5. Vanity: impressions/reach alone, engagement without downstream quality

### Learning **[Documented]**
- ~**50 optimization events** in the week after last significant edit → exit Learning.
- **Learning limited** = unlikely to hit ~50; not a penalty; fix feed of events (budget, audience, rare event, too many ads).
- Significant edits restart learning: targeting, creative, opt event, new ad in set, pause ≥7 days, bid strategy change.

### Leads vs qualified leads **[Documented]**
- **Maximize leads** = volume (contact share).
- **Maximize qualified leads** = CRM-informed quality; Instant Forms + CAPI. New campaigns need CAPI for this goal (from Apr 2026; existing impacted Aug 2026).
- Until CRM→CAPI healthy → Maximize leads + ruthless CRM QA. When healthy → Maximize qualified leads; stage within ~28 days; Meta often cites ~200 leads/mo and ~2-4 weeks training.

### Decision tables (ads)
| Action | When |
|---|---|
| HOLD | Still Learning; spend < ~2-3× target cost-per-business-result; no clear fatigue |
| REFRESH | Creative limited/fatigue; CTR↓ vs this ad’s baseline + frequency↑ |
| KILL ad | Fair spend: weak CTR *and* weak booked/quality vs peers; or fatigue with replacements ready |
| Do not kill | Only because CPL is slightly high in first 2-3 learning days |

### Decision tables (ad sets)
| Action | When |
|---|---|
| HOLD | Learning / Learning limited while consolidating |
| KILL ad set | Post-learning; sustained cost per booked/enroll (or qualified) above kill for ~7+ days or ≥50 events; tracking verified |
| SCALE | Post-learning; at/under target sustained; creative not fatigued; raise budget gradually (big edits restart Learning) |

### Creative volume vs budget **[Opinion]**
If budget can’t feed ~50 events/week, fewer ad sets + rotating creatives beats many starved tests.

### Frequency **[Documented def; Opinion use]**
Impressions ÷ reach. Rising frequency + flat reach + falling CTR + rising cost/result → refresh candidate.

---

## Google (Search / AI Max)

### Hierarchy
1. Primary conversions & value (what Smart Bidding optimizes) **[Documented]**
2. CPA / ROAS vs target (ecom: also CAC vs margin) **[Opinion]**
3. Conversion rate
4. Search terms + landing pages (esp. Final URL Expansion)
5. Lost IS (budget) vs Lost IS (rank)
6. Diagnostics only: Quality Score components, Avg CPC, CTR - QS is **not a KPI / not auction input** **[Documented]**

### Primary vs secondary **[Documented]**
Primary = Conversions column + bidding. Secondary = All conversions only. Soft micros as Primary pollute Smart Bidding.

### Learning **[Documented]**
Smart Bidding ~**7-14 days** / often ≥~30 conversions to evaluate (often ~50 for tROAS). Avoid frequent budget/target/goal edits.

### AI Max **[Documented]**
- Wait **≥2 weeks** after enable before heavy negatives.
- Weak when **budget-limited**.
- FUE can pick other URLs; RSA pins ignored when FUE picks URL. Lock with URL inclusions/exclusions; check landing pages report.

### Decision tables
| Action | When |
|---|---|
| HOLD | New AI Max <~2 weeks or Smart Bidding still Learning |
| NEGATE | Term consistently spends with zero/poor primary conv.; use negatives sparingly on AI Max |
| KILL keyword | Post-learning: high spend, no/poor primary conv., search terms confirm bad intent |
| SCALE budget | Healthy CPA/ROAS + high Lost IS (budget) |
| Fix rank | High Lost IS (rank) → ads/LP/relevance/targets, not vanity CPC |
| FUE exclude | Landing pages report: wrong/thin/non-converting URL |

---

## Local lead gen vs purchase (mapping)

| Business | Judge on | Platform opt |
|---|---|---|
| Local lead gen (e.g. gym Instant Form → booked eval → enroll) | Cost per booked / enroll; lead→booked % | Meta Leads; Maximize leads until CAPI, then qualified leads |
| Purchase / SaaS | Purchase ROAS; CAC vs margin | Sales / Maximize conversion value or tROAS |

Never invent account numbers. Monthly knowledge refreshes must re-check metrics decision rules, not only product UI changes.

## When running this skill
1. Confirm tracking + primary conversion definition.
2. Check Learning status before any kill/scale.
3. Decide with business metrics; use diagnostics only to explain.
4. Label advice [Documented] vs [Opinion].
5. For Achieve/IB specifics, also read current agent memory (quality-first Meta, unit econ, no spend without yes).

skills.name: ads-audit
skills.description: Use when the user wants a Google Ads or Meta audit. Propose only. Findings must clear a money bar and read like a decision, not a dashboard.
skills.instructions:
---
name: Ads Audit
description: >-
  Use when the user wants a Google Ads or Meta audit. Propose only. Findings
  must clear a money bar and read like a decision, not a dashboard.
---
Hunt concrete paid-ads problems. You only propose. Never apply, pause, bid, or delete in this skill.

## Connector
If the Ryze AI connector is missing, stop. Add `https://connector.get-ryze.ai/mcp` (docs: https://www.get-ryze.ai/how-to-connect-claude-to-google-meta-ads-mcp). Wait.

List connections. Use the accounts they named. None named → workspace defaults, and say which.

## Pull
Current vs prior (default last 7 vs prior 7). Slice below campaign: search terms, placements, schedule, device, geo, ads/creatives. Campaign totals are context, not findings.

Google money is micros ÷ 1,000,000. Meta Graph money is often minor units ÷ 100, except Insights `spend` (already whole). Empty or all-zero Insights is not zero spend - recheck the window. Never invent spend, CPA, or ROAS.

## The bar
An empty run is a good run. "Could be better" is not a finding.
A finding needs: exact entity name, real numbers over a real window, a from → to change, honest impact.
Skip paused, ended, zero-delivery. Skip idle cleanup.
Materiality: about $100/month measured waste, or ~3% of monthly spend, whichever is larger.
At most three findings, worst first. One root cause = one finding.

## Hunt, in order
A. Money burning - broken conversion tracking, disapproved ads, search terms/placements with spend and zero conversions, hours/geos/devices with CPA at a multiple of account average.
B. Money missed - converting search terms with no exact keyword; budget-capped campaigns losing impression share to *budget* (not rank) with strong ROAS. Small reversible step, never a double.
C. Hygiene - fatigued creatives, one ad eating all spend, overlapping audiences. Only if it clears the same money bar.

## How a finding reads
Five pieces or it is not a recommendation:
1. Thesis - one sentence, a number from THIS account
2. Evidence - two or three facts with metrics, no adjectives
3. Action - entity, field, from-value, to-value
4. Impact - magnitude + confidence, scoped to a window
5. Watch for - the metric and threshold that would prove it wrong

Title is a claim ("$2.1k/mo on search terms with 0 conversions"). One visual identity. No 20-row tables.

## After the list
Wait for a yes on those exact items. Prefer pause over delete.

# Adult program design guidelines

Full source: `/home/box/agent-data/shared/sc-reference/adult-program-design-guidelines.txt`

## Always (adults ≠ athletes)
- Equipment bias: DB, KB, cables, landmine, TRX, bodyweight first. Barbell/SSB only when training history and quality support it.
- Prefer unilateral over bilateral when in doubt.
- **No** speed, agility, or power blocks unless the coach explicitly asks.
- No competitive season / sport taper logic. Use adult phases: GPP/foundation → hypertrophy → strength (default cycle ~8 wk hypertrophy → 4 wk strength).
- Conservative loading vs athletes at the same training age. Quality over load.

## Session order
SMR (3-5) → breathing (also finish with breathing) → warm-up (5-6 prep + 2 dynamics) → strength (2 primary + 2 secondary in non-competing pairs) → core (1-2, different categories) → tertiary (1).

## Strength rules
- Primary: multi-joint overload; unilateral preferred for adults.
- Pairing: knee-dominant with pull; hip-dominant with push. Never two lowers / two pushes / two pulls.
- Each day: one bilateral lower and one unilateral lower (or vice versa), plus one push and one pull.
- Frequency coverage: 1-4×/week category maps in the source file - open it when building the week.

Re-read the full source before a detailed adult program.

skills.instructions:

name: Advisor persona vs ghostwrite
description: >-
  Use this when an advisor or distilled-persona bot is asked “if you were me,”
  for a take in their voice, or for something to send - fork persona
  (founder-pov) vs ghostwrite (user’s outbound voice).
---
# Advisor persona vs ghostwrite

Use for Elon / Travis / Hormozi / Dan Martell / distilled-persona seats and any bot whose job is to *be* someone. Also use when the user says “if you were me,” “as travis,” “what would X do,” or “write this for me to send.”

## Fork (pick one; say which)

**Persona (default for “if you were me, \<name\>” and “what would you do”)**  
- Speak **as that person**, first person.  
- Use their judgment, priorities, and phrasing from their profile / reference corpus.  
- Advice and opinion are *theirs*, aimed at the user’s situation.  
- Not a draft in the user’s voice. Not sales copy “as if” the user wrote it unless they also ask for a sendable draft.

**Ghostwrite (only when they ask to send, post, email, or “write it in my voice”)**  
- Write **as the user** for an outbound channel (email, Slack, text, caption).  
- Match the user’s real voice and house rules (no em dashes in Achieve/IronBlueprint drafts, etc.).  
- Label it clearly as a draft. Do not send unless send-on-behalf rules are met.

If both are useful: persona take first, then offer a ghostwritten draft in one short line - do not blend them into one ambiguous voice.

## Triggers → mode

| They say | Mode |
| --- | --- |
| “if you were me,” “as \<persona\>,“ “what would you do,” “be blunt” | Persona |
| “write an email/text I can send,” “in my voice,” “draft a reply to …” | Ghostwrite |
| “give me your take, then a message I can send” | Persona, then Ghostwrite as two blocks |

## Rules

1. Never invent quotes or biography for the persona.  
2. Persona mode does not soften into generic coach voice.  
3. Ghostwrite mode does not lecture in the persona’s philosophy unless the user asked for that content inside the draft.  
4. If the request is ambiguous, default to **Persona** for advisor bots and ask once whether they also want a sendable draft.  
5. Sales / Marketing / Copywriter bots stay ghostwrite/outbound specialists; do not steal their job from an advisor seat unless the user pointed the advisor at a draft.

## Anti-patterns

- Answering “if you were me, travis” with a Ryne-voice sales email and no founder-pov take.  
- Signing a ghostwritten draft with the persona’s name.  
- Mixing “I (travis) think…” and “Hey, this is Ryne…” in one message without labeling the switch.

# Athlete program design guidelines

Full source: `/home/box/agent-data/shared/sc-reference/athlete-program-design-guidelines.md`

## Always
- Customize from goals, assessment, training age, chronological age, sport/position/stroke, and season phase.
- Target ~1 hour. Cook before chef - don’t invent a new format.
- Neurological order (most → least demanding):
  1. SMR (3-5 areas from eval/sport)
  2. Breathing (1-2)
  3. Warm-up (5-6 movement prep + exactly 2 dynamics: 1 lower, 1 upper)
  4. Speed/agility when used (1 exercise, max intent, full recovery) - fresh, after warm-up
  5. Power (typically 2: 1 lower + 1 upper) before strength
  6. Strength: 2 primary (heavy compounds) + 2 secondary (lighter/quality)
  7. Core, then tertiary/accessory
- Primary = heavily loaded multi-joint (trap-bar, front squat, chin-up, etc.). Secondary = cables, unilateral balance, bodyweight, isolation.
- Non-competing pairs: knee-dominant with pull; hip-dominant with push.
- Overhead athletes: landmine / horizontal press over true vertical press.
- Programming-room drafts only unless Ryne says to write TrainHeroic. Hawkin first when force plates matter.

Re-read the full source file before a detailed prescription.

skills.description: Use when creating or changing a Grok Bot routine, auditing bot token usage, or deciding whether recurring work belongs on a long chat or a fresh bot.
skills.instructions:
---
name: Cheap routines
description: >-
  Use when creating or changing a Grok Bot routine, auditing bot token usage, or
  deciding whether recurring work belongs on a long chat or a fresh bot.
---
# Cheap routines

Every scheduled wake burns tokens. Pick the coarsest cadence that still delivers the result.

## Cadence

Do not schedule every 15 minutes. That is about 96 runs a day.

Default to hourly, or a few times a day, inside weekday waking hours. Use an event listener instead of a timer when the thing you care about is a Slack, GitHub, or similar event.

Stay quiet when nothing changed. Filler like "(no change.)" still costs a wake.

## Fresh bot for recurring work

A long chat makes every routine more expensive. The model rereads the thread.

Put recurring jobs (digests, inbox sweeps, polls) on a dedicated bot with a short chat. Keep talking to the main bot. That bot does not own the standing timer.

## When you create a bot

If the job is a standing sweep, give it its own bot and one routine at the coarsest useful schedule. Do not hang that routine on a bot whose chat is already long.

Quiet-when-nothing-changed is part of the job, not a courtesy.

skills.name: check-numa-inbox-read-only
skills.description: Use when checking the Numa business-texting inbox (inbox.numa.com) for new or unanswered customer texts - for a brief, a triage pass, or a specific thread. Read-only: read and report, draft replies in chat, never send or type into Numa.
skills.instructions:
---
name: Check Numa inbox (read-only)
description: >-
  Use when checking the Numa business-texting inbox (inbox.numa.com) for new or
  unanswered customer texts - for a brief, a triage pass, or a specific thread.
  Read-only: read and report, draft replies in chat, never send or type into
  Numa.
---
# Check Numa inbox (read-only)

Numa is the business texting inbox at `inbox.numa.com`. There is no connector or public API - access is the signed-in Chrome on your own computer.

**Hard rule: this is a READ pass.** Never click Send, never type into the reply/compose box, never close, assign, snooze, or resolve a conversation. Anything that would go out is written as a draft in chat and waits for the owner to say send on that exact draft. Two past sends leaked stray links because text was typed into the composer early - do not put anything in a send box, not even to "have it ready."

## 1. Open the inbox

Delegate to a `browserUse` subagent (page-level, faster and it does not grab the desktop). Give it the exact URL:

```
https://inbox.numa.com/inboxes/all
```

If the session is live, that loads straight into the list. Login is Auth0: `inbox.numa.com/login` redirects to `login.numa.com/u/login/identifier` (email) then `/u/login/password`.

**If it lands on a sign-in page:** stop the subagent and hand the desktop over with `request_box_help` and one short instruction like "Sign in to Numa". Never ask for, type, or store the password. Once handed back, dispatch the subagent again at the same URL. Sessions persist between checks, so this is occasional, not every run.

## 2. Read the list

Layout when it loads:

- Left rail: **Inbox**, Payments, Reports, Set up, Help, Me
- Folders: **Dashboard**, **All** (unread badge), **You**, **Unassigned**, **@ Mentions**
- Tabs across the top: **Open** (default), **Overdue**, **Reminders**, **Closed**
- Filters: **Assigned to** (All users), **All Labels**, **Sort by** (Newest)

Default read is **All + Open, Assigned to All users**. Each row shows the customer phone number, a one-line summary, the assignee, and a timestamp. Check **Overdue** too when doing a full triage pass - that is where a dropped thread hides.

## 3. Open the threads that matter

Click a row to open it (`/inboxes/all/c/<conversation-id>`). Inside:

- Center: the message history, newest at the bottom. **Scroll up** - the useful context (what was already promised, who last replied) is above the fold, and Numa's automated greeting can sit between real messages.
- Right panel: phone number, **Assigned to**, sentiment, and any **Task** attached to the thread.

Note per thread: who texted, their number, what they actually asked, the last outbound message and who sent it, and how long it has been quiet. Distinguish real inbound questions from Numa's automated greeting and from teammate replies that already answered it.

Use the **Back arrow** at the top left of the conversation panel to return to the list. Repeat for each thread that needs a human.

## 4. Report

Bring back, per thread that needs a reply:

- Name (or number if unnamed) and phone
- What they asked, in one line
- Current assignee and how long it has been quiet
- Whether it is already handled by someone else - if so, say so and do not draft

Then write the reply as a **draft in chat**, in the owner's texting voice, not email voice:

- Always greet: `Hi, FirstName.` - comma after Hi, period after the name. Never skip it, even mid-thread.
- 1-3 sentences. Lead with the answer, not an apology.
- "We" for the business. No email signature, no subject-line structure, no emojis.
- Do not invent prices, availability, or commitments. If a fact is missing (a class has to be checked first), flag it outside the draft rather than guessing.

Before presenting a reply draft as ready, run [Pre-draft check](sand-workflow:pre-draft-check) (name plus phone match, last-48h touches in Quo/Numa and Gmail, future open times, parent only if confirmed, no prices unless read live today).

Apply the same 3-day rule as email: a thread quiet 3 days after an outbound reply gets a follow-up draft surfaced, not a send.

## Never

- Send, reply, close, assign, or snooze anything in Numa
- Type any text, link, or URL into the composer
- Transcribe or store a password or one-time code
- Drive Chrome from the shell (DevTools, Playwright, cookie scraping) - use `browserUse`, or `computerUse` only if the page defeats it

skills.name: cmj-force-time-curve-shape-classification
skills.description: Use when classifying a CMJ propulsive-phase force-time curve shape from raw Hawkin data, or when giving plate-driven training direction from that shape. Sources: Achieve CMJ guide + Kahook/Cressey CMJ Parts 1-2 (phases; graph shape is king).
skills.instructions:
---
name: CMJ force-time curve shape classification
description: >-
  Use when classifying a CMJ propulsive-phase force-time curve shape from raw
  Hawkin data, or when giving plate-driven training direction from that shape.
  Sources: Achieve CMJ guide + Kahook/Cressey CMJ Parts 1-2 (phases; graph shape
  is king).
---
# CMJ Force-Time Curve Classification Guide

**Sources:** Ryne Gioviano / Achieve CMJ Force-Time Curve Classification Guide; Yassir Kahook via Eric Cressey - [Breaking Down the CMJ Part 1](https://ericcressey.com/force-plate-countermovement-jump-1/) (phases) and [Part 2](https://ericcressey.com/breaking-down-the-countermovement-jump-part-2/) (graph shape is king). Use for every plate-driven prescription when a CMJ shape is available. Do not invent a shape; classify from raw Hawkin force-time (session-best). Hand full programs to Coach - this guide informs the plate note and exercise direction only.

## Programming rule (Kahook / Cressey Part 2)

**Shape is king for programming.** Metrics (jump height, peak force, RSI, TTT, EUR) matter for tracking and peer compare - keep them trending the right way - but two athletes with the same height can need opposite emphases. Shape diagnoses *how* they produce force; that drives the next block. Especially true for higher-level athletes where raw vertical force is not always the limiter - efficiency of the signature is.


## Check the jumps before picking exercises

Do this **before** choosing lifts from the progression list. The curve and phase times can ban methods that would otherwise look fine on the sheet.

Plain rules:
- **Shape beats phase time.** A short brake *time* does not mean the stop is good. Late Peak Bimodal / Late Peak Plateau = they do **not** hit the ground hard enough on the catch (low braking RFD by definition). Do not call braking “fine” from time alone.
- If **braking is actually good** (early-peak or healthy bounce *and* short brake time) → **do not** program slow eccentric squats, deep yielding holds for “more brake,” or extra snap-downs / drop-catches aimed at braking.
- If **unweighting is slow** → still train a faster drop. That does **not** cancel Late Peak braking work. Slow drop + late peak = faster get-down *and* a harder stop.
- Match **isometric position to where force hangs** on the curve. Early Peak Plateau / early bimodal hang at the **braking → propulsion** change → use a **quarter-squat Split Squat ISO Push** (overcoming/ballistic). Do **not** default to mid-thigh if the hang is lower.
- Same jump height does not mean the same program - shape decides the emphasis.

Early Peak Plateau example (locked): brake 122 ms + Early Peak Plateau → no long-ecc squat; Day 1 power iso = Split Squat ISO Push at ~quarter-squat, not mid-thigh.

Late Peak Bimodal example (locked 2026-09-11): brake 170 ms looked “fine” on time, but Late Peak Bimodal + EUR ~1.0 = stop is *not* fine. Train the catch (yielding hold / drop-and-stick) plus faster drop. Do not skip braking work.

## Six phases (Kahook / Cressey Part 1)

1. **Quiet / weighing** - still on plate; system reads body weight.
2. **Unweighting** - rapid descent; force below system weight; negative COM velocity; hip/knee/ankle flexion.
3. **Braking** - force returns above system weight while still descending; ends when velocity = 0.
4. **Propulsive** - velocity positive; COM drives up through extension; ends when force → 0 N (takeoff).
5. **Flight** - force ≈ 0 N (air time).
6. **Landing** - positive force returns.

Achieve phase labels used elsewhere (unweight / brake / propulsive) map to 2-4 above.

**Protocol notes (Part 1):** Prefer **hands-on-hips** for standardized lower-body isolation (arm swing adds a second propulsive peak and longer movement time). Cue consistently: *“jump as high as you can, as fast as you can”* - intent for height + speed, not a slow squat-jump.

## How to classify (propulsive phase)

Phases: weighing → unweighting (force < BW) → braking (force > BW while descending) → propulsive (min displacement / v=0 → takeoff) → flight → landing.

Classify on the **smoothed** force trace of the **propulsive** phase (and the braking→propulsion transition for early peaks), as % through propulsion. Require a real trough between peaks before calling bimodal. Peak timing windows:

- **Early peak:** dominant peak in first ~25-35% of propulsion (often at the braking→propulsion transition)
- **Late peak:** dominant peak in final ~40% / later half of propulsion
- **Plateau:** force sustains near peak (>~90%) across a large share of early/mid propulsion rather than a clean peak-and-decline; or a long stretch around peak with no single definitive spike (**Plateau** archetype)

Seven Kahook archetypes below (+ Achieve **Inconsistent** when trial-to-trial shape disagrees). Match the athlete, then use that section’s focus + prescriptions.

---

## Early Peak Unimodal

**Kahook:** One unified peak early. Efficient SSC; strong braking + propulsive working together. Limiter is usually **magnitude**, not quality - make the curve taller and narrower; raise overall output.

**Achieve / focus:** Maintain efficiency while overloading; preserve reactive strength; strength then high-velocity; complex training for transfer-point mechanics; avoid excess volume that disrupts coordination.

**Exercises:**
- Strength: pin/rack → concentric-focused work
- Band-assisted plyometrics for propulsive velocity
- Depth jumps 30-40 cm, GCT <250 ms
- Weighted jump squats 30-45% 1RM, max velocity
- Reactive strength circuits, multi-planar, adequate rest

**Params:** 80-120 contacts/session; strength 3-4×3-5 @ 85-95% 1RM; VBT 0.5-0.75 → 0.9+ m/s mean; maintain propulsive/braking impulse ratio; +2-5% load every 2-3 wk; full recovery between sessions.

---

## Late Peak Unimodal

**Kahook:** Single peak later / more gradual rise toward takeoff. Somewhat efficient SSC; COM controlled. Typical limiter: **low braking RFD** → lower outputs, longer TTT. Program **braking-phase RFD**, not raw strength alone.

**Achieve / focus:** SSC function; RFD eccentric + concentric; braking / elastic storage; unweighting development (phases should be similar in area); systematic reactive strength.

**Exercises:**
- Eccentric + concentric strength for braking RFD
- Drop catch, loaded altitude landings
- Progressive plyos (lower intensity first)
- Depth jumps start 20-30 cm, progress
- Ballistic 40-60% 1RM, velocity focus

**Params:** 60-100 contacts → 120-180; strength 3-4×4-6 @ 75-85% 1RM; VBT 0.5 → 0.9+ m/s; improve unweighting impulse; +5-10 cm drop height every 2-3 wk as technique allows.

**Note:** If unweighting time is the limiter (slow fall; brake already fine), prefer faster drop cues / drop-squat jumps - not slow eccentrics or extra deep yielding isos (Achieve unweighting rule).

---

## Early Peak Bimodal

**Kahook:** Two peaks; higher peak early. High braking RFD; usually higher-output. Second peak = efficiency / COM control breaking down around peak braking; limb and COM velocities out of sync. Strong and fast into the ground; coordination costs the transition into propulsion.

**Achieve / focus:** SSC coupling ecc↔con; cut amortization lag; intermuscular timing; amortization / isometric holds at transition; stability at peak braking.

**Exercises:**
- Ballistic isometrics - brief high-effort at peak-braking position
- Unweighted / band-assisted plyos to cut transition lag
- Rapid SSC, continuous force through the movement
- Velocity-assisted (10-15% BW reduction)
- Reactive progressions, minimal GCT

**Params:** 100-150 contacts, quality first; strength 3-4×3-6 @ 80-90% 1RM with tempo for coordination; VBT 0.5-0.75 → 1.0+ m/s; +5-10% velocity every 2-3 wk as coordination improves.

---

## Late Peak Bimodal

**Kahook:** Two peaks; higher peak late. Lower braking RFD and lower-output than early-peak bimodal. Same coordination/COM-control issue at peak braking **plus** capacity deficit - address **both**.

**Achieve / focus:** Movement re-education; progressive SSC; coordination; eccentric strength + body awareness; unweighting first so braking has a foundation.

**Exercises:**
- Yielding isometrics (ecc strength + awareness)
- Drop squat / drop catch → then propulsive work
- Landing mechanics as foundation
- Progressive plyos from fundamentals
- Assisted movement for coordination
- Targeted strength for force-production gaps

**Params:** 40-80 contacts, quality only; strength 3-4×4-6 @ 80-90% 1RM; VBT 0.5 → 0.75+ m/s; expect 12-20 weeks for meaningful pattern change.

**Locked (Late Peak Bimodal, 2026-09-11):** Do not call braking “fine” from a decent brake *time*. Late Peak Bimodal *is* a braking-quality problem. Pair faster drop (if unweight is slow) with a harder stop (yielding hold or drop-and-stick). Skip slow eccentric squats that teach lingering.

---

## Early Peak Plateau

**Kahook:** Spike early, then flatline. High braking RFD / higher-output (like early bimodal). Plateau flags the same efficiency / COM-control issue around peak braking - force comes on fast, but doesn’t convert into a clean immediate propulsive push.

**Achieve / focus:** Rapid force development; cut neural delay at transitions; amortization / isometric holds at transition; isometric + eccentric for momentum resistance; awareness before complex plyos.

**Exercises:**
- **First pick:** Split Squat ISO Push at ~quarter-squat (overcoming / ballistic) - matches the braking→propulsion hang
- Not mid-thigh by default (that sits higher than this plateau)
- Then: rapid initiation jumps / assisted SSC; cut transition lag
- Ballistic 30-60% 1RM, max velocity
- Awareness → loaded → unloaded plyo only if coordination is still messy

**Params:** 80-120 contacts, max quality; strength 3-4×4-6 @ 75-85% 1RM with pauses; VBT 0.5 → 0.75+ m/s; 2-3 min rest between high-intensity efforts.

---

## Late Peak Plateau

**Kahook:** Flatline first, higher peak later. Lower braking RFD / lower-output. Coordination + capacity - often the group most needing a **two-pronged** approach (build braking capacity + clean coordination).

**Achieve / focus:** Fundamental patterns first; basic reactive systematically; broad strength base; basic amortization / isometric work; body awareness before complex methods.

**Exercises:**
- Yielding isometrics at peak braking (controlled lowering)
- Awareness → loaded → unloaded plyo progression
- Tempo on basic patterns
- Bodyweight mastery before external load
- Basic plyos only (small jumps / simple hops) at first
- Quality-focused resistance training

**Params:** 20-60 contacts, quality only; strength 3-4×6-8 @ 70-80% 1RM, technique first; VBT 0.5 → 0.5-0.75 m/s; 16-24 weeks for fundamental change.

---

## Plateau (Kahook seventh archetype)

**Means:** Long stretch around peak force with **no single definitive spike** - peak effectively across the middle of the graph.

**Kahook:** Efficient SSC; generally strong braking + propulsive. Limiter is magnitude/duration (like early peak unimodal) - raise amplitude, **shorten TTT**, make the curve taller and narrower, raise output.

**Focus / exercises:** Borrow Early Peak Unimodal menu (concentric overload, reactive, weighted jumps) with explicit TTT / narrow-the-curve intent. Do not treat as a coordination-breakdown shape unless a trough or early spike+hold appears (then reclassify to bimodal/plateau early/late).

---

## Inconsistent Pattern (Achieve)

**Means:** High trial-to-trial variability; limited training age / fine motor skill; unstable neuromuscular control across unweighting, transfer, and force production.

**Focus:** General strength foundation; consistency/repeatability; fundamental motor patterns before complexity; simple controlled transfer-point work; basic body awareness.

**Exercises:**
- Iso → ecc → con strength progression
- Fundamental pattern awareness
- Consistent execution over intensity
- Basic strength for consistent reps
- Bodyweight competency before load

**Params:** 20-40 contacts, quality + consistency; strength 3-4×8-12 @ 60-75% 1RM; VBT 0.5 → 0.5-0.75 m/s; 12-20 weeks for basic consistency.

---

## How to use in reports

0. Apply **Check the jumps before picking exercises** (bans first, then picks).
1. Classify the athlete’s latest **session-best** CMJ curve (or note if trials disagree → Inconsistent).
2. Name the pattern exactly as above (prefer Kahook seven + Inconsistent).
3. Plate note = pattern meaning + the 1-2 primary focuses that match their numbers (phase times, EUR, RFD, unweight/brake).
4. Exercise suggestions must come from that pattern’s list - not generic “swimmer” picks. Label off-plate gaps as off-plate.
5. Cite actual Hawkin numbers; do not invent a curve shape Hawkin did not report.
6. Do not write or assign full TrainHeroic programs unless Ryne asks; post direction in chat with Coach and Ryne.

skills.name: cold-email-reply-rules
skills.description: Use when drafting Achieve or IronBlueprint cold first-touch or re-engage sales emails (not booked-eval replies, not pricing replies to inbound questions).
skills.instructions:
---
name: Cold email reply rules
description: Use when drafting Achieve or IronBlueprint cold first-touch or re-engage sales emails (not booked-eval replies, not pricing replies to inbound questions).
---

# Cold email reply rules (Lavender, adapted)

Source: Lavender cold-email findings (Nick Abraham / X, locked for Sales 2026-10-24). Apply to **lead first-touch** and **re-engage** emails only. Do not invent client stories, prices, or results.

## Length and scan

1. Keep under about 75 words; aim for 25 to 50 when the ask is simple.
2. Write at about a 3rd to 5th grade reading level (short words, short sentences).
3. Use 1 to 2 sentence paragraphs (most opens are on a phone).

## Opening

4. Lead with a real observation from their form, sport, age, or prior contact. Never invent one.
5. Turn that observation into a short hypothesis tied to the problem you solve (strength, speed, power, fewer injuries, adult strength / stay active).
6. Double-check every fact before the draft goes out.
7. Focus on their problem or goal, not the facility.

## Proof and tone

8. Use a customer story only when it is real and similar (sport, age, goal). Skip the story if you do not have one.
9. Drop did-you-know stats and informative lecture tones.
10. Cut cliches and soft openers (hope this finds you well, just following up).
11. Light hedge words (might, could) only on cold guesses. Never hedge when answering a direct inbound question: answer first with concrete specifics.

## Ask and subject

12. The goal of a cold or re-engage email is a reply. Make one ask only.
13. Make the question easy to answer (days and times, yes or no, pick a window). Skip open-ended essay questions.
14. Still end with a question plus open time windows when booking is the next step (product lock wins over never ask for a meeting).
15. Subject lines: 1 to 3 words, sound internal. For cold subjects avoid verbs, numbers, questions, and first names when that fits the thread.

## Delivery

16. Leave out images and links in cold and re-engage emails (deliverability).
17. Space sends; do not blast high volume.

## Locks that always win

- Answer first on inbound questions; cut soft openers; concrete specifics; end with a question plus open time windows.
- Achieve lead emails may include one Pricing starts at line only when the price was read live that day from the locked source.
- No prices in ads.
- Never invent client stories or results.
- Pre-draft check before any draft goes to Ryne.

skills.name: design-grok-bot
skills.description: Use this when designing or creating a new Grok Bot, or editing another bot's description. Ask a few preference questions, write a tight persona, CreateAgent, settle a one-word name and the avatar, then verify against the live profile before reporting. Coding bots use pstack / poteto-mode as the quality bar. Mentor/counsel bots default to advice-only (no homework). On a fresh install, run setup-pstack first and ensure healthcheck routines exist.
skills.instructions:
---
name: Design a Grok Bot
description: >-
  Use this when designing or creating a new Grok Bot, or editing another bot's
  description. Ask a few preference questions, write a tight persona,
  CreateAgent, settle a one-word name and the avatar, then verify against the
  live profile before reporting. Coding bots use pstack / poteto-mode as the
  quality bar. Mentor/counsel bots default to advice-only (no homework). On a
  fresh install, run setup-pstack first and ensure healthcheck routines exist.
---
# Design Grok Bot

Create the bot. Do not ship a shareable template unless the user asked for a template.

## Data shape

A bot is four fields, in this order:

1. **One job.** One sentence. What it does every time it wakes.
2. **Anti-jobs.** What it never does, even if asked. Adjacent work goes to a different bot.
3. **Voice.** A few words. Match the user, or a named character. Not a generic assistant.
4. **Wake.** On-demand chat, a standing routine, or both. Quiet when there is nothing to report.

Name is short. Description carries all four. Do not pad with leftover tools, model essays, or "I can also help with..."

`CreateAgent` takes `name` and `description` only. That description is the whole persona. After create, prove it by reading `/home/box/agent-data/agents/<id>/profile.json`. Do not trust the tool ack alone.

There is no delete tool. Only create when the job is real.

## Mentor / counsel bots (default)

If the job is advice, wisdom, mentoring, or philosophy counsel:

- **Advice only.** Give the counsel. Do not end with exercises, journaling prompts, "write down three…", rituals, homework, or "Today’s step" closers unless the user explicitly asks for an exercise.
- Wise-old-mentor craft: hear the question under the question; slow down; one image/proverb then apply; gentle challenge; match length to the wound.
- Never invent quotes.

Sage-class bots follow this by default.

## Fresh install (this bot, after template import)

On the first real user message after this template is imported, do this once before designing anything:

1. Run pstack's setup-pstack skill (`/setup-pstack`) when `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` is missing. Skip if the rule already exists. Do not ask permission. Then `/create-verification-skill` only when a real repo is present and no `verify-*` skill exists.
2. **Prove the standing healthcheck routines exist on this bot.** List `/home/box/agent-data/agents/<this-agent-id>/automations/`. If `transcript-healthcheck` is missing, create it with `update_state` (target `routine`, action `create`): name `transcript-healthcheck`, schedule `44 8 * * 1-5`, prompt pointing at Transcript healthcheck skill, quiet when nothing to propose. If `routine-healthcheck` is missing, create it the same way: name `routine-healthcheck`, schedule `49 8 * * 1`, prompt pointing at Routine healthcheck skill, quiet when nothing to propose. Tell the user what you created (or that both were already there). Do not wait for them to ask. Template import may not materialize packed routines - this step is the safety net.
3. Offer once: "want a checkup of every bot's routines?" Run Routine healthcheck only if they say yes.

Skip steps already done in this chat. Do not re-create routines that already exist.

## Intake

Ask only preference questions no experiment can settle. Typical set, skip any already answered:

- the one job
- voice and name, if they care
- standing routine vs on-demand
- who it talks to (this user, other bots, an outside channel)

Do not ask for tools, plugins, or model if you can copy a working sibling. Do not ask "should I create it?" after the job is clear. Create it.

If the ask is reversible detail (color, a nickname), pick it and say what you picked.

## Coding bots

Bar is pstack. Read pstack's poteto-mode (and boteto-mode on Grok Bot) when writing the persona. pstack is the coding-agent workflow pack: one job, unslopped prose, verified work, CloudAgent for repo work.

Bake into the description:

- one job and anti-jobs
- unslopped, short replies
- repo work goes to a CloudAgent, not a local clone
- slash-skills are live files, not app commands, if this user uses them
- copy the current model rule from an existing coding bot unless the user names one
- point at pstack / poteto-mode as situational, not standing

Do not paste the full pstack playbook into the description.

If pstack is not installed, say so and keep the same tightness anyway.

## Non-coding bots

Same tightness, different job. Scout, shopkeep, life-admin, dispatcher, writer.

Bake into the description:

- ONLY job, named in the first sentence
- stay quiet when there is nothing to report
- never do the adjacent verb (a mentions scout does not post, a drafter does not send)
- the concrete how (which API, which inbox, which channel), not "use whatever tools you have"
- cite or label: only state what was confirmed; never credit a source with more than it said; label guesses as guesses
- relayed approvals: when Chief or Dr. Eggbot relays an approval that quotes Ryne's words, treat it as his yes and do not ask him again

No coding instructions unless the job is hybrid and the split is explicit (coordinate vs write code).

## Name and avatar checklist (before you report back)

The user should never have to check these himself.

1. **Name.** One word that reads like a person or character name, matching the fleet (Sage, Darwin, Hendrix, Maverick). No job titles ("SEO Auditor"), placeholders ("Bot", or "Fuel" until confirmed), or group words ("Boardroom") for a single bot. **Default (Ryne, 2026-10-30):** offer 3 to 5 names drawn from legends in that field (the way Linus and Simon came about), then wait for the pick. Only choose unilaterally when the user said to pick for them or already named one themselves.
2. **Avatar shape** from the fleet scheme: wedge = staff function, square = project manager, blob = data and analysis, tablet = research, heart = social, pebble = single-task tool, teardrop = personal life, shield = security, hex = Chief only. Mentors are exempt.
3. **Avatar color.** Count colors across `/home/box/agent-data/agents/*/profile.json` (`avatarColor`) and pick the least used that fits. Black is Chief only, gray only for temporary bots, never a brown teardrop.
4. **Apply.** You cannot set another bot's avatar. SendToAgent the new bot: run UpdateProfile with `avatar_shape` and `avatar_color` set to the exact values, and reply only to you.
5. **Verify live.** Re-read the bot's `profile.json` and confirm `name`, `avatarShape`, and `avatarColor` match. A bot's "done" is not proof. Only then report the name, shape, and color to the user in one line.

## Editing an existing bot

When the user approves a description change for another bot in your chat, apply it yourself with UpdateAgent and verify the live profile. Do not ask the bot to edit itself: most bots only change their own profile on the user's word in their own chat, which makes the user approve twice. Avatars are the exception (step 4 above).

## After create

Run the name and avatar checklist above, then read the live profile back. Tell the user the name, shape, color, and the one-job line. Mention they delete from the sidebar (right-click, Delete) if they hate it.

If the job needs a standing routine, you cannot write another bot's routines from here. Immediately SendToAgent that new bot with an explicit instruction to call update_state (target routine, action create) with the concrete name, prompt, and schedule or trigger. Do not stop at "set it up in its chat." Confirm to the user that you messaged it to create the routine. If SendToAgent fails, say so and give them the one-line create instruction to paste into that bot.

description: >-

  pricing sheet, ad static, brand kit) for Achieve or IronBlueprint and
